newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing output up 0.3% in Sept.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing output up 0.3% in Sept.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK industrial production in September:
MINING/QUARRYING INCLUDING OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION

NOTE - Consensus forecast was for industrial production to rise by 0.5 percent in September, for a year-on-year rise of 0.2 percent. Manufacturing output was expected to rise 0.5 percent on the month and 0.1 percent year-on-year.
The ONS said in the third quarter of 1996 the majority of manufacturing industries have shown increases in production over the previous quarter.

Most notable were 3.0 percent increases in the output of transport equipment industries, a 1.7 percent rise in textiles, clothing and leather output and a 0.8 percent rise in the output of pulp, paper, printing and publishing industries.
There were, however, decreases of 1.4 percent in the output of non-metallic mineral products and a 1.0 percent fall in the output of coke, mineral oil refining and nuclear fuels industries.

The ONS said the output of durable goods rose 1.3 percent in the latest quarter with increases of 2.3 percent in the output of cars and 0.4 percent in other durable goods output. Durable goods output was 4.1 percent higher than a year ago.
Output of non-durable goods rose 0.4 percent quarter-on-quarter in the third quarter with clothing and footwear output gaining 1.6 percent.
